chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, who said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام say:

'Ali عليه السلام said: The fasting of three days during hajj is one day before al-Tarwiyah, the Day of al-Tarwiyah, and the Day of 'Arafah. So whoever misses that should take the pre-dawn meal on the night of al-Hasbah — meaning the night of al-Nafr — and begin the morning fasting, and [fast] two days after it, and seven when he returns.

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: the day of Tarwiyah, a specified time marker in the hajj rites
key_terms.الْحَجِّ: the pilgrimage during which these fasting days are observed
key_terms.سَبْعَةً: the seven additional days to be fasted upon returning
key_terms.صَائِمًا: being in a state of fasting from the morning
key_terms.صِيَامُ: fasting as a prescribed devotional act
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: the Day of 'Arafah, one of the designated fasting days here
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ النَّفْرِ: the night of departure from Mina, clarifying the intended night
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْحَصْبَةِ: the night of al-Hasbah, identified as an alternative starting time for fasting

ai.seo_question: If someone misses the three fasting days during hajj, when may they make them up?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling for the three compensatory fasting days during hajj, specifying their preferred timing before and during the days of al-Tarwiyah and 'Arafah. If those days are missed, it gives an alternative schedule beginning on the night of al-Hasbah, followed by two more days, and then seven days after returning.
